title: Adjectives + to-infinitive, -ing, that-clause, wh-clause
subtitle: free to leave / busy doing
summary: Choose the pattern that follows an adjective: a to-infinitive, an -ing form, a that-clause or a wh-clause.

lesson.heading: Four patterns after an adjective
rows: You're **free to leave** at any time you want.
(un)able, careful, crazy, curious, difficult, easy, foolish, free, good, hard, impossible, inclined, mad, nice, prepared, ready, stupid, welcome, willing
busy, crazy, foolish, mad, stupid; after the verb *feel*: awful, awkward, bad, good, guilty, terrible
He became **worried (that)** she might fall down.
afraid, alarmed, amazed, angry, annoyed, ashamed, astonished, aware, concerned, disappointed, glad, (un)happy, pleased, shocked, sorry, upset, worried; certain, confident, positive, sure
I'm **not certain (of / about) why** he wants to borrow the money.
afraid, not aware / unaware, not certain / uncertain, doubtful, not sure / unsure, worried
lesson.note: These adjectives come after a linking verb (appear, be, become, feel, seem).

lesson.heading: Adjectives that allow two patterns
rows: to-infinitive or that-clause - all the that-clause adjectives except aware, confident and positive
She was **afraid to say** anything. / I was **afraid that** I would be late.
to-infinitive or -ing - crazy, foolish, mad, stupid
He'd be **stupid to leave** now. / He'd be **stupid giving up** the job.
-ing or that-clause - after *feel*: awful, awkward, bad, good, guilty, terrible
She felt **awful leaving** him with all the clearing up. / She felt **awful that** she was late.

lesson.heading: The fireworks were amazing to watch

left.label: subject + linking verb + adjective + to-infinitive
examples: The top of the jar was **awkward to get off**.

right.label: *It* + linking verb + adjective + to-infinitive
examples: **It was amazing to watch** the fireworks.
**It was awkward to get** the top off the jar.
In informal speech an -ing form is possible: **It was amazing watching** the fireworks.

lesson.note: Also annoying, easy, good, interesting, lovely, simple, terrific, wonderful.

lesson.heading: It + adjective + wh- or that-clause
lesson.text: The same it pattern works with a wh-clause or a that-clause after the adjective.

examples.text: **It is not clear why** he did it.
**It was odd that** she left so suddenly.

lesson.heading: of + subject
lesson.text: After certain adjectives we often put of + subject between the adjective and the to-infinitive. The same idea can be expressed with the person as subject.

examples.text: It was rude (**of them**) to criticise her. / They were rude to criticise her.
It was brave **of her** to spend the night in the old house alone.

lesson.note: Also generous, kind, mean, thoughtful, unprofessional, unreasonable.

lesson.heading: It made me angry ...
lesson.text: To say how somebody reacts to a situation we can use it + make + object + adjective, followed by a to-infinitive, an -ing form or a that-clause.

examples.text: **It made me angry** (to discover) that so much money was wasted.
examples.note: or It made me angry discovering that ... / I was angry to discover that ...

examples.text: **It made me nervous** hearing the dentist's drill as I sat in the waiting room.

lesson.note: Also ashamed, furious, glad, happy, miserable, sad, tired, uncomfortable.

lesson.text: aware, confident and positive take a that-clause, never a to-infinitive: he was confident **that he wouldn't get lost**, not ~~confident not to get lost~~.

exercises.prompt: I'm afraid I can't afford that much. Would you be prepared ___ the price if I pay cash?
exercises.explanation: Prepared is followed by a to-infinitive.

exercises.prompt: He felt good ___ that he had helped solve the problem.
exercises.explanation: After feel + good we use an -ing form, not a to-infinitive.

exercises.prompt: She was too busy ___ on the phone to notice that Roya had come into the room.
exercises.explanation: Busy is always followed by an -ing form.

exercises.prompt: I went into town, but I felt a bit ___ all day.
exercises.explanation: After feel + guilty we use an -ing form (or a that-clause: guilty that I had shopped all day).

exercises.statement: On the bus back to the hotel I got talking to a local woman and was concerned learning that it got very cold in the hills at night.
exercises.explanation: ... and was concerned to learn that it got very cold in the hills at night. Concerned takes a to-infinitive or a that-clause.

exercises.statement: I started to get worried that he might be in danger, but I wasn't certain what to do.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Worried takes a that-clause, and not certain can be followed by a wh-clause.

exercises.prompt: Anyone trying to climb the mountain would be foolish ___ the challenge facing them.
exercises.explanation: Foolish, crazy, mad and stupid take either a to-infinitive or an -ing form.

exercises.prompt: We ended up arguing, but he said that he was ___ lost.
exercises.explanation: Confident takes a that-clause; unlike afraid or worried, it never takes a to-infinitive.

exercises.prompt: I said he was stubborn and that he just ___ that I'd been right.
exercises.explanation: Prepared is followed by a to-infinitive, even in the negative.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite 'Such a magnificent performance was wonderful to hear' beginning with It.
exercises.answer: It was wonderful to hear such a magnificent performance.
exercises.explanation: It + linking verb + adjective + to-infinitive is an alternative to subject + be + adjective + to-infinitive.

exercises.prompt: He criticised the headteacher in front of the staff. It was unprofessional ___ to criticise her like that.
exercises.explanation: After adjectives like unprofessional, kind and mean we add of + object pronoun.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern can follow each adjective?
